role: A one-shot post-v200 classical-reference adequacy audit on the historically exposed p=14kw_size=01 development trajectory. It does not propose a deployable warm initializer and is not fresh validation, external generalization, test evidence, a resource result, or real BOST.
scientific_question: Can one fixed second-order TGV2-PDHG refinement remove the transition-localized gradient failures left by the v200 first-order Huber reference and make the five-camera classical reference adequate on every p14 frame and calibration?
physical_distinction: v201 does not tune the v200 Huber weight, Huber delta, iteration count, normalization, boundary rule, or CGLS depth. It introduces an auxiliary vector field and a symmetric-gradient penalty so affine ramps need not pay the first-order total-variation cost that can bias transition gradients.

primary.gradient: D uses forward-Neumann differences on the physical field axes; spacings are divided by their geometric mean before use

fixed_decision_order: Any binding, isolation, K2 or Huber reproduction, finite, convergence, step-contract, permutation, physical-replay, call-ledger, seal, or independent-comparison failure makes v201 inconclusive.

If the TGV2-PDHG reference fails any strict cell or complete calibration group, conclude FAIL_TGV2_PDHG_REFERENCE_ADEQUACY_V201 and close this exact normalized TGV2 objective and 256-step solver without tuning.

If the TGV2-PDHG reference passes all 1313 cells and 13 groups, conclude PASS_TGV2_PDHG_REFERENCE_ADEQUACY_V201. Because the immutable v199 fixed-identity K1 arm passed only 1268 cells and 3 groups, also record that the fixed-identity tau=2^-8 K1 candidate is closed under an adequate reference.

No v201 outcome authorizes exact-call reduction, wall/RSS, fresh validation, external generalization, curved-ray validity, real BOST, neural training, GPU rental, paper success, first/SOTA/global uniqueness, or algorithm breakthrough claims.
failure_action: Do not tune either TGV weight, their ratio, iteration count, normalization, derivative, boundary rule, step construction, auxiliary initialization, or starting CGLS depth after results.
